title: check_dissector_urls: use the cache for all links
description:
At the moment, the check_dissector_urls.py script uses parallel requests
to check groups of 120 urls. If one of the urls times out, we have to wait
for the timeout to expire before we schedule a new group of requests. The
cache is used to skip urls that have already been checked in a previous
group. If a url appears twice in the same group (and hasn't been checked
before), it is checked twice since all requests are sent at the same time.

This patch changes the overall approach again to reduce the time when
we're effectively blocked and to make better use of the cache.

We store the extracted urls in a python set where duplicate entries are
not allowed. If we add the same url twice, it'll still be listed only
once.

Next, we run through the set and populate the cache. As the urls in the
set are unique, there's no need for groups, we can kick off all requests
at the same time. However, our testing showed that timeouts occur if there
are too many concurrent connections. It should be possible to set a limit
via the TCPConnector, this did not work reliably. We use an additional
semaphore to set a limit of 50 connections.

The final verification of each link in each source file is now done using
the cache.

Finally, the output was refactored to show the urls while the cache is
populated. This takes much longer than reading the urls from the source
files, we should display something while this is ongoing. Also, remove any
reference to cached/uncached now that all urls are cached.

These changes reduce the time for a complete run to below two minutes on
my system.
